purpose: Test whether batched yes/no completeness questions, derived from the task brief and the task category only, predict which recorded answers the blind reviewer rejected, before building any decider into the loop.

decider.sees: task prompt, required finding ids and the answer's summary and findings; never the rubric, source, checker result, arm or verdict

questions.perFinding: Does finding '{id}' give concrete specifics (named functions, files, conditions or cases) for its part of the task, rather than a general statement?
all: Does the answer address every item the task prompt explicitly asks for?
Where the answer describes several steps or checks, does it attribute each to the specific function or component that performs it?
orientation: Does it describe the steps in the order they happen at run time?
diagnosis: Does it explain why the existing check or code path fails to catch the fault, not only what the fault is?
Would the proposed regression test still compile and still exercise the fault after the proposed repair is applied?
impact: Does it state which existing behaviours, guards or tests must remain unchanged?
Does it enumerate the specific new input cases or scenarios tests must add, beyond rewriting existing tests?
Does it state the consequences for existing callers, configuration or stored data?

sample: Every recorded orientation, diagnosis and impact answer with a receipt in the v1, v2, S5 and v3 evidence directories (60 answers, 15 accepted). Code-change tasks are excluded (no answer text).

measures.auc: probability that a rejected answer scores higher than an accepted one, over all answers and over checker-passed answers
measures.anyFlag: answers with at least one 'no', and how many rejections they catch

decisionRule: Build an in-loop decider only if AUC over checker-passed answers is at least 0.75 and any-flag catches at least two thirds of reviewer rejections while flagging no more than half of accepted answers. Otherwise record the result and stop.
biasCaveat: The question author had read the private rubrics and v2/v3 reviewer reasons for these tasks, so the questions may encode rubric knowledge. A passing result here is necessary, not sufficient: confirmation needs fresh held-out tasks whose rubrics the author has not seen.
